_why: M8b deliverable 6: 'Robots class, canonical link and inlined data on the
transaction route are UNCHANGED — a crawler sees exactly what it saw
before.' Its verification asks for the assertion to be made 'against a
stored baseline so the SEO surface cannot regress silently'.
This is that baseline. It is a stored FILE rather than a constant in the
test because the point is that changing the crawl surface has to be a
deliberate edit to a committed artefact that a reviewer sees in the diff —
a literal inside the assertion would move with the code that broke it.
Recorded from the transaction route as it was BEFORE the debug route
existed: `noindex,follow`, canonical at the transaction's own URL, and the
chain-native payload rendered into the page (§7.2 section 8). The debug
route is `noindex` and canonicalises to the transaction — so this
milestone adds no second indexable copy of the same content, which is the
way a new route most easily damages an existing one.
`debugInSitemap` is the half a robots meta tag does not cover. A sitemap
is a SUBMISSION, and SEO-And-Crawl-Budget.md §5's class table gives every
`noindex` class 'Sitemap: No' — so listing the debug route would spend
crawl capacity fetching the transaction's content a second time in order
to be told not to index it. `sitemapRoutes` is what keeps it out, and the
suite asserts the route is still RENDERED, so the two do not get fixed by
dropping the page.
_whyTwoShapes: Page-Descriptions §7.0 makes the transaction route serve the DEBUGGING
INTERFACE where a trace is published, and the metadata page where one is
not. The transaction's own URL therefore has two markup shapes, and this
baseline gained a split rather than a weakening:
`txMustContain`        — required of BOTH shapes. Everything a crawler
was served before and must still be served: the
chain-native payload and §7.2's decoded input,
by the words that name them rather than by the
heading markup that used to carry them.
`txSessionMustContain` — required of the session shape, and the reason
the headings moved: the facts are in §7.1's
metadata pane, in a `<dl class="mddl">` built
by `viewutil.txMetadataRows` — the same single
producer the page's grid uses.
`txPageMustContain`    — required of the metadata shape, which is
unchanged from the recording below.
What did NOT change, and is what the M8b deliverable actually names: the
robots class, the canonical link, and the facts themselves. No `<dt>`, no
cost row and no byte of the native payload left the transaction's URL —
they are rendered inside a pane instead of under an `<h2>`. The test
asserts the `<dt>` set of whichever grid the shape renders against
`txMetadataRows`, so a fact that quietly stopped being served fails here.
